learning_objective: 🎯 See the invisible vibrations! Learn how sound travels, understand pitch and volume, and explore the amazing applications of ultrasound.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: तारत्व (How high or low a sound is)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave. It travels through compressions (particles squeezed together) and rarefactions (particles spread apart). Sound CANNOT travel through a vacuum (like outer space); it needs a medium (solid, liquid, or gas).

Amplitude determines LOUDNESS (bigger wave = louder). Frequency determines PITCH (faster vibrations = higher pitch, like a whistle). Timbre (quality) helps you tell the difference between a piano and a guitar playing the exact same note.
Sound bounces off hard surfaces! An echo is simply a reflected sound. To hear a distinct echo, you must be at least 17.2 meters away from the reflecting surface so your brain can process the delay.

The outer ear (pinna) collects sound. The middle ear has the eardrum and 3 tiny bones that amplify vibrations. The inner ear (cochlea) turns these physical vibrations into electrical signals for the brain.

Humans hear between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz. Below 20 Hz is Infrasound (used by elephants/whales). Above 20,000 Hz is Ultrasound (used by bats, dolphins, and doctors for sonograms to see inside the body).

fun_activity.title: 🥄 The Spoon Bell
fun_activity.instructions: Tie a metal spoon to the middle of a 2-foot piece of string. Wrap the ends of the string around your index fingers and plug your fingers gently into your ears. Lean forward so the spoon swings freely and gently bump it against a table. It will sound like a massive church bell in your head because sound travels better through the solid string than air!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between transverse waves (up and down, like light) and longitudinal waves (back and forth, like sound).
📌 Speed of sound is fastest in Solids, slower in Liquids, and slowest in Gases.
📌 Know the applications of Ultrasound: SONAR (measuring ocean depth), cleaning intricate machine parts, and medical imaging (Echocardiography).
quick_recap: ⭐ Pitch depends on Frequency. Loudness depends on Amplitude.
⭐ The mathematical formula for wave speed is: Speed = Wavelength $\times$ Frequency ($v = \lambda \times f$).
⭐ Reverberation is the persistence of sound in a big hall due to multiple reflections (this is why cinemas have soft, sound-absorbing walls).
